risk.rationale: Case case-003 (s.demir@aegean.edu) does not meet the contain threshold: F1 confirms suspicious sign-ins from Cloudvault VPS (DE) outside baseline (T1078.004) at only 0.52 confidence, and there is no verified downstream account-takeover chain (no MFA changes, mail rules, or exfiltration). It is not benign: F1/F2 are not explained away, and F2 (most sign-ins from DE, LIKELY 0.5) could indicate legitimate travel or attacker origin; it remains unresolved. Monitor is insufficient because F3 confirms an active exposure — VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 runs a product in CISA KEV with multiple CVEs (T1133/T1190) — and the DQ conflict (vpn_session_order failing for vpn-edge-01) prevents reliable session correlation, leaving the evidence conflicting/insufficient. Per the escalate rule (exposure or conflicting/insufficient evidence needing a human), this case requires human triage: patch/isolate the KEV-exposed VPN appliance, verify whether the DE sign-ins belong to the user, and resolve the session-ordering data-quality failure before any contain/benign determination.
